output: If the cumulative value of the contract for an infrastructure project increases by more than ten percent due to amendments, change orders, or other agreements, the winning bidder must post an additional performance security.

instruction: When should negotiations with the first-in-rank consultant be completed?
input: Except for meritorious reasons, negotiations with any one consultant shall be completed within fourteen (14) calendar days.
output: Unless there are meritorious reasons, negotiations with a consultant must be completed within 14 calendar days.

instruction: What is the minimum number of suppliers or contractors to be invited for bidding under alternative methods of procurement?
input: For items (a) and (b) of Section 53, in the case of goods and infrastructure projects, the procuring entity shall draw up a list of at least three (3) suppliers or contractors which will be invited to submit bids.
output: The procuring entity must create a list of at least three suppliers or contractors to invite for bidding when using alternative methods for goods and infrastructure projects.

instruction: What is the primary content of the first envelope for the procurement of consulting services?
input: For the procurement of consulting services: ... 8. A sworn statement attesting compliance to the responsibilities of a Prospective or Eligible Bidder as provided in Section 17.7 of the IRR-A; 9. A sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act in relation to other provisions of RA 3019; and 10. Other information and/or documents specified in the bidding documents.
output: The first envelope for consulting services must include a sworn statement of compliance with Section 17.7 of the IRR-A, a sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act, and other documents specified in the bidding documents.

instruction: What is the rule on confidentiality during the bid evaluation process?
input: Reiterate and emphasize the importance of confidentiality during the bid evaluation process, and the applicable sanctions and penalties, as well as agree on measures to ensure compliance with the foregoing.
output: The pre-procurement conference must emphasize the importance of confidentiality during bid evaluation, including applicable sanctions and penalties, and establish measures to ensure compliance.

instruction: How should the warranty for goods, supplies, and materials be stated?
input: The warranty shall be stated in Philippine Pesos, shall remain effective during the applicable warranty period stated in Section 62.2 of the IRR-A and shall be returned only after the lapse of the said warranty period. The warranty shall be full for the first year, and renewable every year thereafter, subject to depreciation after the first year, on a straight line basis.
output: The warranty should be stated in Philippine Pesos, remain effective for the applicable period, and be returned only after it lapses. It is full for the first year and renewable annually thereafter, subject to straight-line depreciation after the first year.

instruction: What is required of each member of a joint venture for eligibility?
input: Each member of the joint venture shall submit the required eligibility documents;
output: Every member of a joint venture must submit their own required eligibility documents.

instruction: What specific documents are required in the first envelope for infrastructure projects?
input: For the procurement of infrastructure projects: ... 14. A sworn statement attesting compliance to the responsibilities of a Prospective or Eligible Bidder as provided in section 17.7 of the IRR-A; 15. A sworn affidavit of compliance with the Disclosure Provision under Section 47 of the Act in ration to other provisions of R.A. 3019; and 16. Documents/materials to comply with other non-discretionary criteria and requirements as stated in the Instructions to Bidders.
output: The first envelope for infrastructure projects requires a sworn statement of compliance with Section 17.7 of the IRR-A, a sworn affidavit of compliance with Section 47 of the Act, and other documents to meet non-discretionary criteria as specified in the Instructions to Bidders.

instruction: Can a supplier start work under an amendment to order without approval from the head of the procuring entity?
input: Under no circumstances shall a supplier proceed to commence work under any amendment to order unless the same has been approved by the head of the procuring entity concerned or his duly authorized representative.
output: No, a supplier cannot start work under an amendment to order unless it has been approved by the head of the procuring entity or their authorized representative.

instruction: What is the role of the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) in a pre-procurement conference?
input: During this conference, the participants, led by the BAC, shall:
output: The BAC leads the participants in the pre-procurement conference, guiding them through the review and agreement of various procurement aspects.

instruction: What is the `General Appropriations Act`?
input: If not an early procurement activity, select one and delete others: NGA, the General Appropriations Act or Special Appropriations. GOCC and GFIs, the Corporate Operating Budget. LGUs, the Annual or Supplemental Budget, as approved by the Sanggunian.
output: The General Appropriations Act (GAA) is the primary source of funding for National Government Agencies (NGAs) that are not early procurement activities.

instruction: What does the `Bid Security` clause require of a bidder?
input: The Bidder shall submit a Bid Securing Declaration or any form of Bid Security in the amount indicated in the BDS, which shall be not less than the percentage of the ABC in accordance with the schedule in the BDS . . . Any bid not accompanied by an acceptable bid security shall be rejected by the Procuring Entity as non-responsive.
output: The Bidder is required to submit a Bid Securing Declaration or a form of Bid Security with an amount not less than a specified percentage of the Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC), as indicated in the Bid Data Sheet (BDS).

instruction: Who can audit a contractor's accounts and records?
input: The Contractor shall permit the GOP or the Procuring Entity to inspect the Contractor’s accounts and records relating to the performance of the Contractor and to have them audited by auditors of the GOP or the Procuring Entity, as may be required.
output: The Government of the Philippines (GOP) or the Procuring Entity can inspect and audit a contractor's accounts and records related to their performance on a project.

instruction: What should a bidder check before submitting its bid?
input: The Bidder, by the act of submitting its Bid, shall be deemed to have inspected the site, determined the general characteristics of the contracted Works and the conditions for this Project, such as the location and the nature of the work; (b) climatic conditions; (c) transportation facilities; (c) nature and condition of the terrain, geological conditions at the site communication facilities, requirements, location and availability of construction aggregates and other materials, labor, water, electric power and access roads; and (d) other factors that may affect the cost, duration and execution or implementation of the contract, project, or work and examine all instructions, forms, terms, and project requirements in the Bidding Documents.
output: Before submitting a bid, a bidder should inspect the site, assess all physical and environmental conditions that may affect the project's cost and duration, and thoroughly examine all instructions, forms, terms, and requirements in the Bidding Documents.

instruction: What is the purpose of the `Bill of Quantities` (BoQ)?
input: The objectives of the Bill of Quantities are: to provide sufficient information on the quantities of Works to be performed to enable Bids to be prepared efficiently and accurately; and when a Contract has been entered into, to provide a priced Bill of Quantities for use in the periodic valuation of Works executed.
output: The Bill of Quantities serves two main purposes: to provide detailed information on work quantities for accurate bid preparation, and to provide a priced list for the periodic valuation of completed work after a contract is awarded.

instruction: How should a bidder prepare their bid to comply with the Bidding Documents?
input: Bidders shall submit offers that comply with the requirements of the Bidding Documents, including the basic technical design as indicated in the drawings and specifications.
output: A bidder's offer must fully comply with all requirements in the Bidding Documents, including the basic technical design detailed in the drawings and specifications.

instruction: What can a procuring entity do if a bidder fails to provide 'as built' drawings or operating and maintenance manuals on time?
input: If the Contractor does not provide the Drawings and/or manuals by the dates stated above, or they do not receive the Procuring Entity’s Representative’s approval, the Procuring Entity’s Representative may withhold the amount stated in the SCC from payments due to the Contractor.
output: The Procuring Entity's Representative may withhold a specified amount from the contractor's payments if 'as built' drawings or manuals are not provided or approved by the required date.

instruction: What are the rules regarding partial bids?
input: If the Project allows partial bids, all Bids and combinations of Bids as indicated in the BDS shall be received by the same deadline and opened and evaluated simultaneously so as to determine the Bid or combination of Bids offering the lowest calculated cost to the Procuring Entity. Bid Security as required by ITB Clause 15 shall be submitted for each contract (lot) separately.
output: If partial bids are allowed, all bids must be submitted by the same deadline, opened, and evaluated simultaneously. A separate bid security must be submitted for each contract or lot.

instruction: What is `PhilGEPS`?
input: PhilGEPS - Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System.
output: PhilGEPS stands for Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System.

instruction: What is the main role of the `Glossary of Terms, Abbreviations, and Acronyms` section?
input: Glossary of Terms, Abbreviations, and Acronyms
output: The glossary provides definitions for key terms, abbreviations, and acronyms used throughout the Philippine Bidding Documents.

instruction: What are the mandatory documents to be submitted in the technical component envelope?
input: The first envelope shall contain the eligibility and technical documents of the Bid as specified in Section IX. Checklist of Technical and Financial Documents .
output: The first envelope, which is the technical component envelope, must contain all the mandatory eligibility and technical documents listed in Section IX of the checklist.

instruction: What is the purpose of the `Bid Data Sheet`?
input: The Bid Data Sheet (BDS) consists of provisions that supplement, amend, or specify in detail, information, or requirements included in the ITB found in Section II, which are specific to each procurement.
output: The Bid Data Sheet (BDS) provides specific details, amendments, or supplements to the general information and requirements outlined in the Instructions to Bidders (ITB) for a particular procurement.

instruction: What must be included in the `Detailed Estimates Form`?
input: Duly accomplished Detailed Estimates Form, including a summary sheet indicating the unit prices of construction materials, labor rates, and equipment rentals used in coming up with the Bid; and Cash Flow by Quarter.
output: The Detailed Estimates Form must include a summary sheet detailing the unit prices of construction materials, labor rates, and equipment rentals used for the bid, as well as a Cash Flow by Quarter.

instruction: What is the primary purpose of the Philippine Bidding Documents (PBDs) for Consulting Services?
input: These Philippine Bidding Documents (PBDs) for the procurement of Consulting Services through Competitive Bidding have been prepared by the Government of the Philippines (GoP) for use by all branches, agencies, departments, bureaus, offices, or instrumentalities of the Government, including government-owned and/or -controlled corporations (GOCCs), government financial institutions (GFIs), state universities and colleges (SUCs), local government units (LGUs), and autonomous regional government.
output: To serve as a mandatory document for the procurement of Consulting Services through Competitive Bidding by all branches and instrumentalities of the Government of the Philippines.

instruction: What law governs the mandatory use of the Philippine Bidding Documents (PBDs)?
input: The procedures and practices presented in this document have been developed through broad experience, and are for mandatory use in projects that are financed in whole or in part by the GoP or the World Bank or any foreign government/foreign or international financing institution in accordance with the provisions of the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act 9184 (R.A. 9184).
output: The PBDs are for mandatory use in accordance with the 2016 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act 9184 (R.A. 9184).

instruction: What key information should the Bidding Documents define?
input: The Bidding Documents shall clearly and adequately define, among others: (a) the objectives, scope, and expected outputs and/or results of the proposed contract; (b) the minimum eligibility requirements of bidders, such as track record to be determined by the Head of the Procuring Entity; (c) the expected contract duration, delivery schedule and/or time frame; and (d) the obligations, duties, and/or functions of the winning bidder.
output: The Bidding Documents must define the contract's objectives, scope, expected outputs, minimum eligibility requirements for bidders, contract duration, delivery schedule, and the obligations and duties of the winning bidder.

instruction: Which parts of the PBDs contain provisions that should be used unchanged?
input: In order to simplify the preparation of the Bidding Documents for each procurement, the PBDs groups the provisions that are intended to be used unchanged in Section II. Eligibility Documents of Part I; and Section II. Instructions to Bidders (ITB) and Section IV. General Conditions of Contract (GCC) of Part II.
output: Provisions in Section II. Eligibility Documents, Section II. Instructions to Bidders (ITB), and Section IV. General Conditions of Contract (GCC) are intended to be used unchanged.

instruction: Where should data and provisions specific to a particular procurement be included?
input: Data and provisions specific to each procurement and contract should be included in Section III. Eligibility Data Sheet (EDS) of Part I, Section III. Bid Data Sheet (BDS), and Section V. Special Conditions of Contract (SCC) of Part II.
output: Specific data and provisions for a contract should be included in the Eligibility Data Sheet (EDS), Bid Data Sheet (BDS), and Special Conditions of Contract (SCC).

instruction: What should the final Bidding Documents not contain?
input: The final documents should contain neither blank spaces nor options.
output: The final Bidding Documents should not contain any blank spaces or options.

instruction: What should be done to the cover of the Bidding Documents?
input: The cover should be modified as required to identify the Bidding Documents as to the names of the Project, Contract, and Procuring Entity, in addition to date of issue.
output: The cover must be modified to identify the Project's name, Contract, Procuring Entity, and the date of issue.

instruction: How long does a Bidder have to submit its latest tax returns and other documents after receiving a notice that it submitted the Lowest Calculated Bid?
input: Within a non-extendible period of five (5) calendar days from receipt by the Bidder of the notice from the BAC that it submitted the Lowest Calculated Bid, the Bidder shall submit its latest income and business tax returns filed and paid through the BIR Electronic Filing and Payment System (eFPS), and other appropriate licenses and permits required by law and stated in the BDS.
output: A bidder has a non-extendible period of five calendar days from receiving the notice of having the Lowest Calculated Bid to submit its latest income and business tax returns and other required licenses and permits.

instruction: What is the policy on foreign language documents submitted by a bidder?
input: If the eligibility requirements or statements, the bids, and all other documents for submission to the BAC are in foreign language other than English, it must be accompanied by a translation in English, which shall be authenticated by the appropriate Philippine foreign service establishment, post, or the equivalent office having jurisdiction over the foreign bidder’s affairs in the Philippines. For Contracting Parties to the Apostille Convention, only the translated documents shall be authenticated through an apostille pursuant to GPPB Resolution No. 13-2019 dated 23 May 2019. The English translation shall govern, for purposes of interpretation of the bid.
output: Foreign language documents must be submitted with an authenticated English translation. For parties to the Apostille Convention, only the translated documents need to be authenticated via apostille. The English translation will be used for interpreting the bid.

instruction: What must be included in the list of a contractor's key personnel?
input: A List of Contractor’s key personnel (e.g., Project Manager, Project Engineers, Materials Engineers, and Foremen) assigned to the contract to be bid, with their complete qualification and experience data shall be provided. These key personnel must meet the required minimum years of experience set in the BDS .
output: The list must include the name, designation, and complete qualification and experience data for key personnel like the Project Manager, Project Engineers, and Foremen. These personnel must meet the minimum experience requirements in the BDS.

instruction: What are the rules regarding the use of notes and footnotes in the final Bidding Documents?
input: This Preface and the footnotes or notes in italics included in the Invitation to Bid, BDS, General Conditions of Contract, Special Conditions of Contract, Specifications, Drawings, and Bill of Quantities are not part of the text of the final document, although they contain instructions that the Procuring Entity should strictly follow. . . These notes are intended only as information for the Procuring Entity or the person drafting the Bidding Documents. They should not be included in the final Bidding Documents.
output: The Preface and italicized notes and footnotes, which are intended as information for the Procuring Entity, should not be included in the final Bidding Documents.

instruction: Under what circumstances can a contract be terminated for other causes?
input: Contract termination shall be initiated in case it is determined prima facie by the Procuring Entity that the Contractor has engaged, before, or during the implementation of the contract, in unlawful deeds and behaviors relative to contract acquisition and implementation, such as, but not limited to corrupt, fraudulent, collusive, coercive, and obstructive practices as stated in ITB Clause 4.
output: A contract can be terminated if the Procuring Entity determines that the contractor has engaged in unlawful deeds and behaviors such as corrupt, fraudulent, collusive, coercive, or obstructive practices related to contract acquisition and implementation.

instruction: How is the contractor's liability treated if it's a joint venture?
input: If the Contractor is a joint venture, all partners to the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable to the Procuring Entity.
output: If a contractor is a joint venture, all partners are jointly and severally liable to the Procuring Entity.

instruction: What happens if a contractor fails to submit an updated Program of Work within the specified period?
input: If the Contractor does not submit an updated Program of Work within this period, the Procuring Entity’s Representative may withhold the amount stated in the SCC from the next payment certificate and continue to withhold this amount until the next payment after the date on which the overdue Program of Work has been submitted.
output: If a contractor fails to submit an updated Program of Work on time, the Procuring Entity's Representative can withhold a specified amount from the next payment certificate until the overdue document is submitted.

instruction: What is the purpose of the 'Program of Work'?
input: The Contractor shall submit to the Procuring Entity’s Representative for approval the said Program of Work showing the general methods, arrangements, order, and timing for all the activities in the Works.
output: The Program of Work outlines the general methods, arrangements, order, and timing for all project activities and must be submitted to the Procuring Entity's Representative for approval.

instruction: What are the rules regarding payments for materials and equipment delivered to the site?
input: Except as otherwise stipulated in the SCC, materials and equipment delivered on the site but not completely put in place shall not be included for payment.
output: Unless the Special Conditions of Contract (SCC) state otherwise, materials and equipment delivered to the site that are not yet installed or in place are not eligible for payment.

instruction: What is the role of the Special Conditions of Contract (SCC)?
input: The Special Conditions of Contract (SCC) complement the GCC, specifying contractual requirements linked to the special circumstances of the Procuring Entity, the Procuring Entity’s country, the sector, and the Works procured. . . Amendments and/or supplements to provisions of the GCC as necessitated by the circumstances of the specific purchase, must also be incorporated.
output: The SCC complements the GCC by specifying contractual requirements unique to the specific project and Procuring Entity, and it may include amendments or supplements to the GCC provisions.

instruction: What is the requirement for bidders regarding their key personnel and major equipment?
input: The Bidder must provide a List of Contractor’s key personnel (e.g., Project Manager, Project Engineers, Materials Engineers, and Foremen) assigned to the contract to be bid, with their complete qualification and experience data. . . A List of Contractor’s major equipment units, which are owned, leased, and/or under purchase agreements, supported by proof of ownership, certification of availability of equipment from the equipment lessor/vendor for the duration of the project, as the case may be, must meet the minimum requirements for the contract set in the BDS .
output: Bidders must provide a list of their key personnel with their qualifications and experience data, as well as a list of major equipment units, including proof of ownership or availability certification, that meet the minimum requirements set in the BDS.

instruction: What must be included in the Detailed Estimates Form?
input: Duly accomplished Detailed Estimates Form, including a summary sheet indicating the unit prices of construction materials, labor rates, and equipment rentals used in coming up with the Bid; and Cash Flow by Quarter.
output: The Detailed Estimates Form must include a summary sheet with the unit prices for construction materials, labor rates, and equipment rentals used to create the bid, along with a Cash Flow by Quarter.

instruction: What is the required payment currency for a contract?
input: Payment of the contract price shall be made in: [Select one, delete other/s] Philippine Pesos. [indicate currency if procurement involves a foreign-denominated bid as allowed by the Procuring Entity, which shall be tradeable or acceptable by the BSP.]
output: Payment for the contract is typically made in Philippine Pesos, or in a tradeable currency accepted by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) if a foreign-denominated bid is allowed.

instruction: How can a bidder acquire further information about a project?
input: For further information, please refer to: [Insert name of officer] [Insert name of office] [Insert postal address] and/or [Insert street address] [Insert official electronic mail address] [Insert telephone number, indicate area code] [Insert facsimile number] [Insert website address, if applicable]
output: A bidder can get more information by contacting the designated officer at the Procuring Entity's office, using the provided postal address, email, telephone, or website.

instruction: Who can request a clarification or amendment to the Bidding Documents?
input: Prospective bidders may request for clarification on and/or interpretation of any part of the Bidding Documents. Such requests must be in writing and received by the Procuring Entity, either at its given address or through electronic mail indicated in the IB , at least ten (10) calendar days before the deadline set for the submission and receipt of Bids.
output: Prospective bidders can request clarification in writing, which must be received by the Procuring Entity at least ten calendar days before the bid submission deadline.

instruction: What is a 'Contractor'?
input: Contractor is a natural or juridical entity whose proposal was accepted by the Procuring Entity and to whom the Contract to execute the Work was awarded. Contractor as used in these Bidding Documents may likewise refer to a supplier, distributor, manufacturer, or consultant.
output: A Contractor is an individual or legal entity whose bid was accepted and who was awarded the contract to execute the work. The term can also refer to a supplier, distributor, manufacturer, or consultant.

instruction: What information should the cover of the Bidding Documents include?
input: The cover should be modified as required to identify the Bidding Documents as to the names of the Project, Contract, and Procuring Entity, in addition to date of issue.
output: The cover of the Bidding Documents should be modified to include the names of the Project, Contract, and Procuring Entity, along with the date of issue.

instruction: Who is responsible for the acts of a subcontractor?
input: The Supplier will be responsible for the acts, defaults, and negligence of any subcontractor, its agents, servants, or workmen as fully as if these were the Contractor’s own acts, defaults, or negligence, or those of its agents, servants, or workmen.
output: The Contractor is fully responsible for the acts, defaults, and negligence of its subcontractors, agents, or workmen.

instruction: What is the purpose of the 'Notes on the Special Conditions of Contract'?
input: The clauses in this Section are intended to assist the Procuring Entity in providing contract-specific information in relation to corresponding clauses in the GCC found in Section IV. The Special Conditions of Contract (SCC) complement the GCC, specifying contractual requirements linked to the special circumstances of the Procuring Entity, the Procuring Entity’s country, the sector, and the Works procured.
output: The notes are meant to help the Procuring Entity provide contract-specific information and ensure that the SCC complements the GCC by addressing the special circumstances of the project.

instruction: What does the 'Scope of Bid' section of the Instructions to Bidders describe?
input: The Procuring Entity, [indicate name] invites Bids for the [ insert Procurement Project ], with Project Identification Number [indicate number]. The Procurement Project (referred to herein as “Project”) is for the construction of Works, as described in Section VI (Specifications).
output: The 'Scope of Bid' section identifies the Procuring Entity, the Procurement Project, and its Project Identification Number, and specifies that the project is for the construction of Works as detailed in the Specifications section.

instruction: What happens if a bidder fails to provide an updated Program of Work on time?
input: If the Contractor does not submit an updated Program of Work within this period, the Procuring Entity’s Representative may withhold the amount stated in the SCC from the next payment certificate and continue to withhold this amount until the next payment after the date on which the overdue Program of Work has been submitted.
output: If a contractor fails to submit an updated Program of Work on time, the Procuring Entity's Representative can withhold a specific amount from the next payment certificate and subsequent payments until the document is submitted.
